SEIL shares rose about 3% on the news; this figure is reported by the article rather than attributed as a verified market outcome.
items.title: BSE cleared SEIL's restructuring plan ahead of GREW Energy listing

items.summary: The leaders of China, the US and Russia met for 90 minutes on Nov 19 at an APEC side event in Shenzhen, issuing a joint declaration pledging talks on nuclear risks, energy supply cooperation and UN reform. Analysts say all three walked away claiming gains: Xi gained hosting prestige as a convening power; Trump projected global leadership and put nuclear arms control on the agenda; Russia's status was elevated with its top-level isolation from the US effectively ended, reinforced by declaration language protecting state officials' immunities amid Putin's ICC warrant. The declaration offered no timetable, mechanisms or plan for follow-up meetings. Analysts differ on whether closer coordination bolsters global stability or grants the three greater sway: Chong Ja Ian of NUS read Xi's references to core interests and red lines as implying a three-way division of the world, while Wu Xinbo of Fudan saw it instead as addressing shared challenges without dividing spheres of influence. On nuclear risks specifically, experts view talks rather than cuts as the realistic near-term outcome: Salisbury of IISS notes New START expired in February 2025 and that modernisation makes reductions unlikely on a long road; Wu suggested preventing AI control over nuclear weapons could be discussed. Stockholm International Peace Research Institute estimates China holds about 620 warheads versus roughly 5,042 for the US and 5,420 for Russia. Concrete action remains thin: Wang Dan of Eurasia Group called the energy pledge a possible positive spillover but noted it specified no quantities or timetable; Putin said leaders had not agreed to meet regularly in this format, though Wu believes further rounds could occur within two years.
items.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen produced a joint declaration with no binding commitments

items.summary: In an interview, Peter Gabriel discusses his 13-track, nearly 90-minute album o:i, its two versions produced by Tchad Blake and Mike 'Spike' Stent, and his promotion of AI as a creative tool. He asserts that AI will ultimately do things better than humans in music, though he adds caveats about the dangers of AI and robots in warfare and calls for international agreements with guard rails on algorithm release; these views are attributed to him rather than established fact. He also describes collaborations involving bonobo Kanzi communicating musically via sign language and a speech-synthesis keyboard developed by primatologist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, Michael Levin's work on morphogenesis including growing an eye on a frog leg, experiments suggesting plant sentience at MIT, and plans for brain-computer interfaces he calls becoming cyborgs. His track record of anticipating industry shifts is cited as supporting his forward-looking views: being the first British artist to own a sampler in the early 1980s, co-founding a streaming platform that competed with Spotify, and leaving Genesis when progressive rock became too grandiloquent; these are presented as past events. The interview notes o:i continues the project begun with i/o (2023), his first new material in 21 years, including songs like A Hard Lesson started in 1989 while he was a mainstream pop star after So shifted more than 5m copies in the US alone; these figures are reported as stated. Gabriel attributes his lengthy album-making process to being easily distracted and valuing diverse interests over finishing quickly.
items.title: Peter Gabriel interview covering his new album o:i and his advocacy for AI in music

items.summary: Honda unveiled the Avancier, a six-seat flagship hybrid SUV slated for sale next spring in Japan, China and Australia but not the U.S., where its sales fell 53% in September. Built mainly in Thailand with an undisclosed price, it will sit above the CR-V as the first model using Honda's new drivetrain pairing a more powerful engine with a more efficient electric motor. The launch is part of Honda's plan to introduce 15 new gas-electric models by March 2030 and its pivot away from fully electric cars after ill-timed EV investments triggered a ¥2.5 trillion ($15.7 billion) impairment charge and the company's first annual loss; it also plans a $3 billion Ohio factory for next-generation hybrids. Product planner Junichi Miyahara said Honda wants to strengthen its foothold in large vehicles, where its share trails competitors, while analyst Tatsuo Yoshida warned that abandoning EVs entirely could expose Honda as demand shifts again.
items.title: Honda launches hybrid Avancier SUV as it pivots from EVs

items.summary: City authorities reported that Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv on Friday killed three people and damaged two bridges, according to the mayor. The attack followed Vladimir Putin's vow of 'much more painful' retaliation after Ukraine this week struck the Crimea bridge connecting Russia-annexed Crimea to mainland Ukraine. A separate liveblog entry reports US envoy Jared Kushner told President Volodymyr Zelensky he believes Russia is comfortable with NATO-like security guarantees for postwar Ukraine, while a third entry describes a summit in Shenzhen attended by Xi Jinping, Putin and Donald Trump where Putin said the three nations share interests in settling regional conflicts including Ukraine's.
items.title: Russian attacks killed three and damaged two bridges in Kyiv

items.summary: Dr Yanagizawa-Drott and Olaf Willner used an AI verifier on 1,000 APE (artificial production of economic) papers and found none error-free: 842 contained at least one severe error, some invalidating headline results. The Economist partnered with Refine to review 100 randomly chosen papers from the top five journals published in the first nine months of 2026 using several frontier AI models plus a human check; this flagged 4,158 issues and found at least one grave error in about one in ten papers. The two exercises are not directly comparable, but the lower rate among human economists suggests people retain an edge. Alexis Akira Toda of Emory University found that for economic-theory papers AI lowers the cost of checking a candidate flaw but does not yet reliably substitute for the human judgment that locates the flaw initially; another study comparing APE and published papers attributed most differences to ideas rather than execution. Michele Zampa of the Geneva Graduate Institute, grading 981 AI papers against 41 human ones on research-question novelty and acknowledgment of methodological limitations, found AI outperformed in crowded fields while humans performed at a constant level regardless of literature size. Benjamin Kohler of ETH Zürich and colleagues had AI reproduce 48 social-science papers from raw data and a methods description; discrepancies between originals and reproductions were roughly equal for AI and human work, but the balance tilted against humans as model quality improved.
items.title: AI verification finds errors in economics papers; human economists still show an edge

items.summary: A University of Liège team modeled one representative semi-detached dwelling, selected from 708 audited homes and calibrated against four years of measured gas and electricity use. Adding a 5 kWh battery to an existing heat pump and rooftop PV reduced annual grid imports from 40.0 kWh/m² (solar alone) to 33.2 kWh/m², a drop of 6.8 kWh/m² or 17%, while net annual energy use stayed identical across the three solar-plus-storage configurations. Operational emissions fell by another 14% versus solar alone. Battery capacity gains show diminishing returns: the first 2 kWh saved 0.43 kg CO₂e per square meter per year, and expanding to 5 kWh added only 0.31 over that range; at 5 kWh the home already used 95% of its own generation, leaving little surplus for a larger battery under this control strategy. The researchers tested two sizes rather than pin down a precise threshold. Replacing the gas boiler with a heat pump gave the largest single carbon cut (67%), and adding PV plus the 5 kWh battery brought total operational emissions from 18.46 to 4.64 kg CO₂e per square meter per year, or 75% overall. Grid imports remained concentrated in winter evenings when solar output was insufficient. The study did not quantify electricity bill savings or investment payback; the reported figures are model-based estimates for one building and depend on heating demand, fuel replaced, heat pump efficiency, solar output, and local hourly emissions, so results do not generalize beyond this case.
items.title: Heat pump plus solar-plus-storage retrofit cuts grid electricity imports by 17% in a Belgian home model

items.summary: Sean Cairncross, the US national cyber director who advises the president on cybersecurity policy and strategy while coordinating cyber efforts across federal agencies, was dismissed from his role following a series of technology outages affecting travel, communications, banking, and an internal National Security Agency system. A source close to the White House told AFP that Kirsten Davies, currently acting as principal advisor for information management, IT, cybersecurity, and information assurance to Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, will take over on a temporary basis; State Secretary Marco Rubio posted congratulations on social media. The office was first established in 2021, and the Trump administration released a seven-page cyber strategy document in March pledging to disable cyber threats through streamlined regulations, modernised federal systems, hardened infrastructure, and AI advantage.
items.title: US national cyber director Sean Cairncross fired after wave of tech outages

items.summary: The Chinese embassy in Japan warned its nationals on Tuesday to avoid climbing Mount Fuji during the closed season, citing strong winds and blizzards with no operational shelter or first-aid facilities. The warning follows the disappearance of Chen Jie, 25, who vanished on 8 November while attempting an ascent alone after his two companions turned back; his family is reportedly offering 500,000 yuan ($75,000) for information leading to his recovery and 100,000 yuan if his body is found. The embassy's concern is that the large reward could encourage ill-prepared climbers to attempt dangerous off-season ascents; Mount Fuji's official climbing season runs from around early July to early September. Separately, Yamanashi prefectural authorities announced earlier this year that rescues by helicopter for off-peak climbers will be self-funded and that detailed climbing plans will be required, with governor Kotaro Nagasaki stating these measures aim to change perceptions of winter climbing. On Wednesday, Nagasaki said search efforts could trigger "secondary disasters" and appeared to appeal directly to Chen's family via a Mainichi Shimbun report, urging them not to endanger others; some Japanese social media users have similarly expressed fears the reward may tempt reckless climbers. Yamanashi police reported that Chen pressed on alone from the fifth station of the Yoshida Trail at around 2,300m after his friends turned back, and a friend last heard from him via video message at 10:30; authorities launched a search on 10 November but had to halt it several times due to poor weather. The reward figure is reported by Chinese and Japanese media without confirmation of when Chen's father posted the offer.
items.title: Chinese embassy warns citizens against off-season Mount Fuji climbs amid missing climber's reward

items.summary: Nepal observes Kaag Tihar, a festival honoring house crows as divine messengers, but Kathmandu's human-crow relations face strain from habitat loss and unmanaged refuse. Satellite analysis attributes a 124% expansion to urban sprawl between 1989 and 2018, while another study found municipal green space fell by 54% between 1975 and 2025; the removal of more than 2,000 mature trees along major roads has pushed crows (Corvus splendens) to nest on utility poles. Bird ecologist Hem Bahadur Katuwal attributes this shift to habitat destruction leaving only adaptable generalist species like crows behind. Unmanaged refuse—open dumping and uncovered meat-shop waste—has drawn dense crow and black kite concentrations, with ornithologist Kamal Raj Gosai noting that exposed food accelerates their crowding while crows serve as scavengers feeding on carcasses. This aggregation fueled an H5N1 outbreak at Nepal's Central Zoo linked to wild crows moving across the city, causing loss or culling of more than 60 animals; veterinarian Krishna Prasad Acharya says crows occupy an unusual ecological niche spanning garbage dumps, poultry farms, and human settlements that escalates cross-species disease risk. Katuwal argues eliminating urban crows is misguided since they clean waste, placing the blame on poor waste management and habitat destruction rather than the birds themselves. Kathmandu acting mayor Sunita Dangol reports incorporating bird conservation into environmental policy by removing decorative tree lights, adjusting road plans to preserve mature trees, and developing planting guidelines with botanists.
items.title: Kathmandu's urban sprawl and waste are reshaping crow populations ahead of Kaag Tihar

items.summary: The Yorke and Northern Local Health Network (YNLHN) announced it would discontinue a one-team, one-site birthing model at the Jamestown and Crystal Brook hospitals, abandoning the trial about one month into its planned six-month run. The change followed local clinicians advising they would not participate; GPs had written to the health minister with "urgent concern" that the rostering restricted doctors from holding maternity and emergency on-call roles simultaneously while complicating handovers. YNLHN governing board chair John Voumard said the trial aimed to address workforce shortages and non-compliance with SA Health rostering requirements, which he said were met at only these two sites in the state; he insisted compliant rosters require five doctors per site per roster 365 days a year and that this requirement would not change. Both hospitals will continue birthing services only when they meet the rostering requirement. SASMOA chief industrial officer Bernadette Mulholland said practitioners did not agree with the network's "rostering position" and described it as "unsustainable." SA Health had paused birthing services for one month in June over a workforce shortage, and there were 41 diversions from Jamestown and Crystal Brook between July 2025 and June 2026. A petition against the trial attracted more than 10,000 signatures before closing; Member for Stuart Geoff Brock said he would table it in parliament next week seeking an inquiry into the YNLHN board amid community frustration over communication. Private midwife Chrissy Mackinnon described herself as "absolutely thrilled" by the reversal but agreed that lack of clear communication was a significant issue, while Voumard attributed wider community concerns to misinformation and said birthing families would face uncertainty under the previous system unless there were more local doctors and midwives.
items.title: SA Mid North birthing-model trial abandoned after community backlash

items.summary: A severe storm cell on Thursday 19 November 2026 destroyed two transmission towers on the 132 kV line between Cultana and Port Lincoln, according to a state of emergency declaration. Transmission operator ElectraNet reported about 24,000 customers lost power regionwide; by Friday's update roughly 10,000 properties remained without supply while crews worked temporary solutions that could take several days. Energy Minister Tom Koutsantonis declared an electricity supply emergency under the Energy Management Act 2004 for a period of 14 days unless revoked earlier, authorizing use of a diesel generator in Port Lincoln and directing AEMO to seek spare generation. Because Port Lincoln had become islanded from the National Electricity Market, SAPN asked households there with rooftop solar panels to switch them off until advised otherwise so they would not trip the temporary generators; Koutsantonis said this advice did not apply outside that region. The incident prompted comparisons to the 2016 statewide blackout caused by a cascading failure after storm damage in the Mid North, though MP Sam Tefler noted this event was more localized and raised questions about energy security once restoration completes.
items.title: South Australia declares electricity supply emergency after storm damages transmission infrastructure

items.summary: Large demonstrations in the Czech Republic challenged Prime Minister Andrej Babiš's plans to change the funding model of public broadcasters. Mikuláš Minář, Chair of the Million Moments for Democracy movement, joined François Picard from Prague on Spotlight, warning that his country risks following Hungary and Slovakia into democratic backsliding by citing their leaders Orbán and Fico as models to avoid. Marking the anniversary of the 1989 Velvet Revolution, Minář recalled the freedoms gained after communism's fall and called for stronger opposition parties and continued public mobilisation. He clarified that his group is a civil movement rather than an electoral party.
items.title: Czechs protest against Babiš's public broadcaster funding changes amid democracy concerns

items.summary: The Delhi High Court sought written responses from the Enforcement Directorate, Bureau of Immigration, and Serious Fraud Investigation Office regarding whether a look-out circular has been issued against Tina Ambani. Justice Mini Pushkarna issued notices after she filed a disclosure petition seeking confirmation on any LOC ahead of her planned departure for Thailand, the UAE, Oman, and Bhutan on December 10. Her counsel, Arshdeep Singh Khurana, told the court that no summonses were currently pending from either agency; he sought to have any existing LOC disclosed or its absence placed on record before she travels. In her petition, Ambani expressed concern that an SFIO LOC might stem from its investigation into Reliance Group companies or that an ED LOC could relate to a money-laundering probe under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. She cited summonses received in February by the ED and on July 20 under Section 217 of the Companies Act, 2013 by the SFIO, which she responded to through written communications and her lawyers; she also wrote to the Bureau of Immigration on August 28 seeking confirmation but reported receiving no response. She argued that being kept unaware of an LOC's existence would bar any legal challenge, characterizing this as a violation of natural justice and Articles 14, 19, and 21 of the Constitution. The underlying investigations concern loans exceeding ₹40,000 crore obtained by Anil Dhirubhai Ambani Group companies from public and private sector banks, with investigators suspecting diversion through complex financial transactions; the ED's probe also examines a suspected trail linked to a luxury condominium purchase in Manhattan. No LOC has been confirmed as existing—only that its status is being sought—and no response had been filed by any agency at the time of reporting.
items.title: Delhi HC seeks ED and SFIO responses on whether an LOC exists against Tina Ambani before her planned December travel abroad.

items.summary: The US Commission on International Religious Freedom alleged Thursday that India is targeting Muslim citizens during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls (SIR), removing them from voter lists, labeling them 'foreigners,' and deporting them. The commission's head Asif Mahmood attributed these claims to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who called three crore removed voters 'Bangladeshi infiltrators' on November 2 and referred to India's Muslims as 'infiltrators.' Commissioner Gene Mills characterized the expulsion of citizens based on Muslim faith as a religious-freedom escalation. The commission recommended that the US Department of State designate India a country of particular concern, though its suggestions are non-binding; it had made this recommendation in its 2026 annual report too. The Ministry of External Affairs has not responded but previously dismissed the panel's assessments as biased and politically motivated, while Indian ambassador Sharjeel Imam—detained over six years in an untried 2020 Delhi riots case—urged the commission to introspect its 'prejudices.' Separately, the SIR itself is contested: conducted across phases from Bihar (2025) through 19 states and Union Territories by mid-2026, it has drawn opposition claims of mass voter deletion, Supreme Court confirmation of legality without letting the Election Commission decide citizenship, BJP-state use of results to deny ration cards and passports, and nationwide protests since October 2 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.title: US religious freedom panel alleges India targets Muslims in electoral roll revision

items.summary: On November 19, the International Court of Justice ruled in Gambia v Myanmar that the Tatmadaw's attacks on the Rohingya met the legal definition of genocide under the 1948 UN Genocide Convention. The court found specific intent to destroy the group by concluding that the pattern, selective targeting and lethality of the attacks could not plausibly be explained as a counterinsurgency operation (at least 10,000 Rohingya are thought dead; roughly 750,000 fled to Bangladesh). The ruling is described as unprecedented in three ways: it found for the first time that a state committed genocide rather than merely failed to prevent it; it imposed obligations on Myanmar toward victims—reparations and compensation, safe voluntary return, restoration of citizenship after 1982 legislation rendered them stateless—and investigation into individual criminal responsibility (linking the case to the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant for Min Aung Hlaing and national universal-jurisdiction courts); and it accepted Gambia's "erga omnes partes" standing argument. The author attributes a key consequence: accepting that legal tool opens a pathway for other Genocide Convention cases, most significantly South Africa v Israel over alleged genocide against Palestinians in Gaza. Enforcement is limited because the ICJ has no enforcement arm; the Myanmar government cannot be compelled to comply, but reputational damage and support for sanctions, financial restrictions, arms-sale prohibitions and other cooperation limits are described as likely consequences (the author frames these as probable rather than certain). The article notes a weakened international legal environment over 20 years and an ICC "under siege by the Trump administration," presented as context. Judge Iwasawa Yuji read the judgment; thousands in Bangladeshi refugee camps reportedly chanted "Thank you Gambia."
items.title: ICJ finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya; ruling may shape Israel case

items.summary: Nearly 1,689 David Jones employees were served redundancy notices on Friday, with employment set to terminate December 30. The redundancies follow the retailer's entry into voluntary administration earlier in the month and its announced closure of 19 of its 38 stores across Australia and New Zealand on November 11. Union SDA NSW secretary Bernie Smith said it would seek alternative employment for members, noting companies had already come forward to offer roles; the union also established a help desk over entitlements. Retail analyst Gary Mortimer called the news 'deeply disappointing' and warned that losing around 1,500 positions would add pressure on Australia's labour market as its unemployment rate sits at 4.9 per cent. The ABC confirmed David Jones is up to date with superannuation for its 6,000 employees under new pay-day laws from July; the company said customers' entitlements will be paid but delivery options such as click and collect are unavailable while online orders surge amid longer expected deliveries.
items.title: David Jones redundancy notices issued to nearly 1,700 staff amid Christmas-period closure

items.summary: At the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen, industry executives reported that global investors are shifting from treating Chinese assets as short-term trading opportunities toward holding them for asset allocation and long-term returns. He Yiwei, CEO of Zhong Ou Asset Management International Limited, attributed this to China's financial opening-up expanding its share of the global economy and said overseas long-term investors including sovereign wealth funds have steadily increased their investments; he also called for wider access to cross-border products and more consistent Asia-Pacific rules for digital connectivity and green finance. Ho Yiu-tung, co-CEO of JPMorgan China, characterized China's opening as moving beyond expanded market access toward closer alignment with international rules, noting the bank has operated in the country for 105 years; he cited that China has the world's second-largest stock and bond markets. Ernesto Torres Cantu, Citi's head of international, said APEC member economies' trade grew sharply over the past decade to about half of global trade, creating cross-border sourcing, sales, and investment opportunities. These are claims made by executives at a summit; none were independently verified in the text.
items.title: Executives say global investors increasingly treat Chinese assets as long-term holdings at 2026 APEC CEO Summit

items.summary: Kolkata recorded roughly 35 mm of rainfall between 8:30 AM and 5:30 PM on Thursday as Cyclone Akvan's outer bands brought continuous rain, per The Telegraph. The India Meteorological Department issued a yellow watch for heavy rainfall over Kolkata and adjacent districts until 2 PM Friday, November 20, warning of thunderstorms with winds of 30-40 km/h and up to 7-11 cm of rain across six areas; IMD attributes the stronger impact on Bengal to Akvan's projected landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha being closer than previous cyclone landfalls. AccuWeather separately forecasts a maximum around 23 degrees Celsius, minimum 21 degrees Celsius, wind gusts up to 70 km/h, and roughly 9 mm of rain over 5.5 hours on Friday with a 91% precipitation probability; it projects heavier evening rainfall (13.7 mm) and overnight totals (13.4 mm). The Telegraph reports that South 24-Parganas, East Midnapore, West Midnapore, Jhargram and Bankura face very heavy rain warnings, with some areas possibly receiving up to 200 mm within 24 hours; AccuWeather instead forecasts only light rain on Saturday (rising to 27 degrees Celsius), sunshine Sunday (31 degrees Celsius), returning thunderstorms Monday November 23, and improved conditions Tuesday. The two sources disagree materially: IMD warns of heavy rainfall across six districts while AccuWeather's district-level forecast is limited to Kolkata with modest totals; the article presents Akvan's northward track as an established fact rather than a forecast, though it was described as expected landfall near Gopalpur.
items.title: Cyclone Akvan triggers yellow rain alert across Kolkata and neighbouring districts

items.summary: Pakistan Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik visited New Delhi for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum, drawing criticism from Congress and other opposition parties over his past threats toward India. The central government and Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat defended hosting him as consistent with multilateral protocol, noting that all member nations were invited to the cultural summit.
items.title: India hosts Pakistan's climate change minister at SCO civilisational forum amid opposition criticism

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur police arrested two accused and recovered jewellery, valuables, tools, and a motorcycle worth approximately Rs 45 lakh in the theft of Sanjeev Jain's residence at Mahavir Colony under Mandi police station. The complaint was registered on November 17 after gold and silver jewellery belonging to the daughter-in-law, along with cash and other items, went missing; SSP Abhinandan formed joint teams from Mandi police station, SOG, SWAT, and the surveillance cell. Two accused were arrested on November 19 following a tip-off near Baba Laladas Road: Chona alias Mujammil of Muzaffarnagar's Civil Lines area, with around seven criminal cases against him in Saharanpur and Muzaffarnagar, and Salim from Roorkee residing at Khata Khedi. Police attributed the 24-hour resolution to CCTV analysis and surveillance inputs rather than any single investigative method; they described the entry as jumping a boundary wall behind the property and entering the kitchen through an exhaust fan slot opening. SSP Abhinandan announced a Rs 25,000 cash reward for the joint teams involved.
items.title: Saharanpur police recover Rs 45 lakh stolen from jeweller within 24 hours

items.summary: Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai announced on Friday that Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra (Balen) Shah will undertake a state visit to India from November 22 to 23 at the invitation of Indian PM Narendra Modi. A 34-member government delegation led by Shah is scheduled to depart Kathmandu for New Delhi, with a delegation-level meeting between the two prime ministers set for Monday followed by joint project inaugurations in energy and bilateral cooperation agreements. The itinerary also includes a call on President Droupadi Murmu, wreath-laying at Rajghat's Mahatma Gandhi memorial, and attendance at the Nepal-India Business Forum. The visit is framed against India-Nepal ties rooted in historical bonds, the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, a 1,751-kilometre open border, and an adage describing shared livelihoods; these are described as evolving toward pragmatic economic, energy, and digital integration under Nepal's new leadership. The relationship framing is presented by the source rather than independently established.
items.title: Nepal PM Balen Shah to make state visit to India, November 22-23

items.summary: Analytics platform Sensor Tower estimates GTA 6's pre-orders and first-day sales reached more than 24.5 million units, worth about $2.36bn (£1.8bn), making it the largest entertainment launch in history; this figure is an estimate from email receipts data rather than a confirmed total, since Rockstar and parent company Take-Two have not released official sales details but described demand as "unprecedented." For context, Sensor Tower notes that this first-day gross exceeds Spider-Man: Brand New Day's $2.5bn cinema run only over the game's single day versus the film's entire release window, so the comparison is of different scopes rather than a direct tie. The PlayStation 5 accounted for around three quarters of sales with Xbox covering the balance. Niko Partners separately forecasts more than $3bn in worldwide sales this year and estimates that GTA 6 will still fall short of 1939's Gone with the Wind, which has made an estimated $4.5bn adjusted for inflation; both are projections rather than measured results. The game is estimated to have cost over $1bn to develop, making it potentially the most expensive video game in history, though this remains an estimate and a claim of record status. Sensor Tower also projects that GTA 6's popularity will reduce time spent on other single-player titles by 10%, which is another forecast rather than observed data.
items.title: GTA 6 estimated to be biggest entertainment launch after first-day sales top $2.3bn

items.summary: Sensor Tower estimates GTA 6 generated $2.36 billion in revenue from pre-orders and launch-day sales on its November 19 release, with 24.58 million copies sold by Thursday evening; these figures are the platform's own estimates rather than confirmed data. Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two have not published official numbers, though demand has been described as "unprecedented." For comparison, Take-Two reported that GTA V generated more than $800 million in retail sales during its first 24 hours (excluding Japan and Brazil launches) and shipped nearly 235 million copies overall. The article's revenue figure is an estimate from a third-party analytics firm; the official figures remain unverified by the game's developer or publisher.
items.title: GTA 6 estimated launch revenue and sales per Sensor Tower, unconfirmed by Rockstar or Take-Two

items.summary: Sean Cairncross is leaving as White House national cyber director following a week of technology-related service disruptions affecting air travel, banking, communications and e-commerce, including the National Security Agency. Secretary of State Marco Rubio named Kirsten Davies to succeed him in an acting capacity; she was previously the Pentagon's Chief Information Officer. Officials say there is no evidence of a cyberattack, attributing the outages instead to technology failures. Cairncross had been nominated by Trump and confirmed by the Senate in 2025 for his role as top adviser on cybersecurity and data protection policy.
items.title: White House replaces national cyber director after tech outages

items.summary: The White House named Department of War chief information officer Kirsten Davies as US national cyber director, replacing Sean Cairncross. The appointment comes against scrutiny over widespread service outages at Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, air traffic control and the National Security Agency that disrupted travel, bank access and classified communications; even Trump allies accused officials of withholding causes. Davies reportedly holds nearly two decades in cybersecurity after roles as Unilever's chief information security officer, plus positions at Estée Lauder, Barclays-Africa, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Siemens, and she founded the Institute for Cyber nonprofit. She became Department of War CIO on December 23, 2025, following Senate confirmation, advising the defence secretary on cyber matters while overseeing its strategy and budget. Accounts of Cairncross's departure conflict: Axios reported he declined another two-year term to allow time before Democrats take control in January, describing it as amicable, while CNN cited a White House source saying Trump supported firing him for lacking strong cyber credentials. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth welcomed the appointment, citing her dedication and confidence she would advance Trump's agenda; Trump dismissed the outages with "things like that happen," and Rubio said there was zero information linking them to a malicious actor. JPMorgan Chase attributed its incident to third-party providers targeted in a cyberattack, which Fox News linked to a ransomware group called Non-profit claiming responsibility for leaking data tied to JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard.
items.title: Trump names Kirsten Davies as national cyber director amid service outages

items.summary: At the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, on November 20, 2026, leaders released two documents calling for greater regional connectivity and fewer trade barriers. The APEC Connectivity Blueprint emphasized strengthening land, maritime and air transport networks and called for digital transformation of transport systems, including exploring safe autonomous technologies; it reaffirmed the forum's commitment to the Putrajaya Vision 2040. In a separate statement titled the 2026 APEC Leaders' Shenzhen Outlook, leaders acknowledged complex global challenges alongside emerging opportunities and pledged to maintain macroeconomic stability while promoting productivity and economic growth. The documents describe these commitments as voluntary, nonbinding and consensus-based; they do not establish binding obligations or report specific infrastructure investments.
items.title: APEC leaders call for stronger regional connectivity at Shenzhen summit

items.summary: Heavy fighting occurred along a key route through Port-au-Prince as Haiti's National Police, with the UN-backed anti-gang task force and private firm Vectus Global, conducted an operation in Martissant on Thursday that killed at least 34 suspected gangsters. The police posted footage of armoured vehicles moving through the neighbourhood, which local media described as having heavy gunfire and explosive drones; the area has been overrun by gangs for five years since rival groups began fighting to control it in 2021. Police said operations are entering a new phase aimed at increasing pressure on gang networks, dismantling strongholds, and extending control over strategic areas including Tabarre in Port-au-Prince and the Artibonite region. El Salvador also deployed about 2,500 troops to Haiti last month after four of their own went missing following an attack on 18 October; under President Nayib Bukele's orders they recently attacked two gang leaders' homes but neither Jeff nor Lanmò San Jou was killed.
items.title: Haitian armed forces launch Martissant operation killing at least 34 suspected gang members

items.summary: The FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup opened on 19 November 2026 in Qatar. The article states this is the second time Qatar has hosted the tournament, after its first hosting in 2025, and claims it will host for five consecutive years through 2029—presented as a plan rather than an established fact. This edition features 48 teams and more than 104 matches across the full competition; on opening day alone, eight matches were played with Uganda and Egypt among those in action, and more than 10 African nations are competing to improve on previous results.
items.title: FIFA U-17 Men's World Cup opening day in Qatar, 2026

items.summary: Per a report by The Information, Meta intends to sell its pocket-sized Muse Charm AI device at $300 with up to 12 months of free 5G data from Verizon. These figures come from an unnamed source and are unconfirmed; Reuters could not immediately reach Verizon for comment, while a Meta spokesperson declined specifics but said the company would share more soon. The roughly two-inch (5-cm) device carries Muse, an AI agent unveiled in September by CEO Mark Zuckerberg that lets users delegate tasks such as shopping, travel booking and form-filling directly through taps on its screen without relying on smartphone apps. A built-in 5G modem enables access to Muse even without Wi-Fi, though the device cannot make calls. Meta frames the gadget as part of a broader effort to reduce dependence on Apple and Google operating systems by building its own AI platform. The launch is expected in time for December's holiday shopping season, according to Zuckerberg at Connect.
items.title: Meta plans $300 price and 12 months of free Verizon 5G for Muse Charm AI device

items.summary: Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar was reportedly admitted to a private hospital in Chennai on Wednesday night, with sources indicating he is likely to remain under medical observation for about two days. No official confirmation came from Lok Bhavan. DMK president MK Stalin spoke by phone to inquire about his health and wished him a speedy recovery, per a party release.
items.title: Tamil Nadu Governor Arlekar hospitalised; Stalin wishes recovery

items.summary: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that Japan Tobacco's decision to cut its dividend would not hinder the government's industrial investment programme. The government owns a 37.55 per cent stake in Japan Tobacco and draws on dividend income from the company for such funding. Katayama told a news conference, "Even after the revision to the dividend forecast, there is no possibility that industrial investment will be hindered." Japan Tobacco lowered its annual dividend forecast by 25 per cent and expects a loss after losing control of Russian subsidiaries when President Vladimir Putin ordered their seizure in October; those units had accounted for around 25 per cent of group profits. Shares slumped more than 8 per cent early on Friday. The government booked 156 billion yen ($977.02 million) from its JT holdings into a special account for the year ended in March, at an exchange rate of $1 = 159.6700 yen.
items.title: Japan's finance minister says JT dividend cut will not disrupt industrial investment plans

items.summary: A tiger was seriously injured after a passing car hit it near Khatgaon Phata close to Sindewahi on the Nagpur highway in Maharashtra's Chandrapur district on Thursday around 10.15 am. Per Lokmat, Ashish Sudhakar Santoshwar of Ballarpur reported that the animal pounced on his two-wheeler while crossing the road before colliding with a car carrying him and family travelling from Nagbhid to Chandrapur; the driver reportedly stopped immediately after impact. A video circulating on social media shows the injured tiger lying in bushes beside the highway, with a gathered crowd allegedly making noises to provoke it as the animal bares its teeth but stays put without charging. The incident raised concerns about how people behave around vulnerable wild animals. After initial care at Savargaon, the tiger was shifted to the Transit Treatment Centre (TTC) in Chandrapur for further treatment.
items.title: Injured tiger struck by car near Khatgaon Phata, Chandrapur; onlookers reportedly provoking it

items.summary: Brent crude traded at $92.67 per barrel and WTI at $83.06 per barrel, reversing an earlier-week decline after reports that Yemen's Houthis struck targets in Riyadh including the financial district and sovereign wealth fund headquarters plus a Jubail petrochemicals company, alongside IRGC claims of daily tanker mine strikes in the Strait of Hormuz this month with two reported explosions on Thursday. These developments counter supply-glut narratives: the International Energy Agency predicted an oil surplus returning this quarter extending into next year, while investment banks claimed oversupply as Persian Gulf exports rebounded to pre-war levels and exceeded them. Oil and gas flow trackers dispute that view, noting exports have improved since early in the war but remain below pre-war levels and may have declined after a September peak amid tightened strait transit enforcement in October and November.
items.title: Crude prices rebound on Houthi attacks and Strait of Hormuz tanker incidents

items.summary: ACME Solar Holdings Limited reports that its wholly owned subsidiary ACME Sigma Urja Private Limited commissioned a Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) facility of 57.69 MW on November 19, 2026, in Kharnai village under Rawatbhata tehsil in Chittorgarh district, Rajasthan. The site combines 100.02 MW of installed solar capacity with a Battery Energy Storage System rated at 57.69 MW / 265.38 MWh and is connected to the Neemuch Pooling Station for power evacuation. ACME Solar states that BESS integration will store electricity generated by solar arrays so it can be dispatched when required, thereby improving supply flexibility and grid reliability; this characterization of benefit is a company claim rather than an independently verified outcome. The commercial operation date (COD) was scheduled for November 21, 2026, and the company reports securing a Power Purchase Agreement with NHPC Limited to sell renewable electricity from the project. This commissioned phase represents one stage toward completing ACME Solar's larger 250 MW FDRE project; the text frames it as an important step but does not establish that completion is assured or on schedule.
items.title: ACME Solar commissions 57.69 MW FDRE capacity in Rajasthan with BESS, COD set for November 21, 2026.

items.summary: Anthropic opened its Nasdaq debut on November 19 at a share price of $111.50, about 34% above the Wednesday IPO price of $83, then pared gains to close at $97.17, up 17%. Its fully diluted valuation reached approximately $2 trillion while its market value based on outstanding shares peaked around $1.5 trillion; this figure edged past SpaceX's June listing and made Anthropic the first frontier AI company to go public. The article frames these figures as a benchmark moment amid cooling enthusiasm for AI stocks, without establishing that the debut itself confirmed sector stability. Bob O'Donnell of TECHnalysis Research said the launch reassures the market but is only the beginning, citing OpenAI, Nvidia and data-center conditions as unresolved factors; Talley Leger of The Wealth Consulting Group called it not a prudent buy-at-any-price opportunity for retail clients, noting first-day IPO buyers have historically underperformed broader indexes over three years. On profitability, Anthropic's net loss narrowed in the third quarter even as revenue jumped 47% from the prior quarter with sharply slowed growth; CEO Dario Amodei said the company hopes to reach investment grade and use debt at some point in the future while facing nearly $900 billion in computing commitments. The article attributes these claims to reporting rather than presenting them as settled outcomes.
items.title: Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO reached an approximate $2 trillion valuation, edging past SpaceX

items.summary: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO did not stop a broad decline in AI-linked stocks, as global equity markets fell sharply. Asian markets were on track for their worst week since 2020: Taiwan's index dropped 6.7% with TSMC down about 6%, Japan's Nikkei fell 5%, and South Korea's Kospi lost 5.5%. SoftBank shares fell 14.5% in Tokyo amid concerns over its AI bets, marking its worst day in more than two years. Europe was heading for its worst week since March, with the Stoxx 600 down 1.3% early Friday, and Britain's FTSE 100 hit a five-month low after dropping 4.8% on the week. The sell-off followed Wall Street losses Thursday when all main indices fell over 2%. Anthropic shares rose 17% at launch after briefly surging nearly 40%, but were heading for Friday losses, down 6% to $91.30 near the IPO price of $83. Daniela Hathorn of Capital.com said demand for AI exposure remained strong but was insufficient to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability, and sustainable investment spending; she noted that selling pressure had spread beyond a few technology giants and Europe's recent outperformance had faded.
items.title: Global stock markets slumped after Anthropic's IPO failed to halt an AI sell-off

items.summary: Anthropic's first-day IPO gain of around 17%, closing at just over $97 with a nearly $1.3tn market capitalisation and $1.75tn fully diluted valuation, did not allay investor concerns about an AI bubble; the stock fell by 4.7% in after-hours trading to $92.60 before dropping further in pre-market trading on its second day. Asian markets sold off overnight led by chip companies: Taiwan's index dropped 6.7% for a weekly loss of more than 16%, with TSMC down about 6%; South Korean stocks fell more than 5% to their lowest in over nine months, with Samsung Electronics and SKHynix both falling about 7%. The MSCI EM Asia equity index is down more than 4% on the week after losing nearly 9%, putting it on track for its worst week since mid-March 2020. DeutscheBank's Jim Reid noted Hong Kong's Hang Seng was approaching bear-market territory, down almost 20% from January's peak; the CSI 300 fell 1.85%, Shanghai Composite 2.10%, and Australia's S&P/ASX 200 1.58%. The risk-off tone extended to gold sliding to a 14-month low of $3,625 an ounce after falling 2.68% on the day, Bitcoin down 1.25% to its lowest since early July, and US high-yield credit spreads widening by 6 basis points to 344bps, their widest since May. Interactive Investor's Richard Hunter attributed weakness in the AI trade to heavy capital investment, possible datacentre slowdowns linked to a recent Democratic sweep, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation raising questions about China-US national security; he said there is no doubt AI is here to stay but heady valuations have raised doubts about payback timing. Separately, California served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia over whether advanced chip exports reached China in contravention of US restrictions, with state attorney general Rob Bonta citing concerns that the company may have misled investors after Huang's resignation following revelations of personal conduct including a relationship with Alice Huang; Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said the IPO strengthens the company financially. SoftBank shares fell more than 14% on their worst day since August 2024 amid worries about its AI bets, and OpenAI reportedly slashed a $10bn fundraising target last month. In UK data, ONS public sector net borrowing was £17bn in October, higher by around £800m year-on-year against forecasts of £18bn; the financial year to date figure stood at £111.3bn, down £7.3bn from a year earlier. Retail sales rose 0.7% month-on-month in October after households stockpiled emergency supplies following government advice.
items.title: Asian stocks head for worst week since 2020 as Anthropic IPO fails to end AI sell-off

items.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia, issued Thursday, into whether advanced semiconductor chips exported by the company reached China in breach of US restrictions. The investigation also examines whether Nvidia or former CEO Jensen Huang passed confidential information to China and misled investors about that risk; Bonta said the conduct raised "bright red flags" but did not assert any wrongdoing occurred. The subpoena follows Huang's resignation a week earlier after revelations he had multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang of Megaspeed, which has bought nearly $5bn (£3.8bn) of Nvidia chips and hardware in recent years and is itself under investigation for possibly diverting restricted chips to China; Megaspeed says it is "legitimate and lawful" and that Huang left late last year. Nvidia shares fell about a fifth since Huang admitted the affair, reaching a one-year low on Thursday's close and wiping almost $1tn off market value. Harvey Jones, Nvidia's chair, said earlier in the week the company had no intention of reinstating Huang despite calls from Elon Musk and other tech figures; Huang is due to testify before congressional committees about potential national security breaches on 1 December. Separately, AMD shares closed down nearly 8% after reports linked by short seller Hunterbrook Media warned of its China links and "circular financing" of customers, with a further fall of more than 5% in pre-market trading; the allegations concern use of AMD software by a US-blacklisted Chinese server maker and datacentre lease guarantees for unsold cloud capacity. AMD said the reports misrepresent its practices and that it complies with export control laws; its market capitalisation is reported as more than $800m, though this figure appears inconsistent with the company's stated scale.
items.title: California subpoenas Nvidia over possible China chip exports and investor deception

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India issued frequently asked questions on Friday to clarify how foreign exchange reporting rules, which took effect October 1 after being notified in January, apply to services trade. The central bank had earlier exempted resident individuals from declaration requirements and set a ₹0.1 crore ($10,760.79) threshold for certain obligations; the RBI clarified that this threshold applies per inward remittance rather than to aggregate receipts. Non-individual service exporters receiving more than ₹0.1 crore must file an export declaration form before the credit of proceeds, and authorised banks may extend filing deadlines if they judge exporters' reasons justified while being required to publish trade-related policies on their websites. In a statement, the RBI said the regulations aim to align with evolving global trade practices and enhance ease of doing business.
items.title: RBI clarifies forex reporting rules for service imports and exports

items.summary: At the European Banking Congress in Frankfurt on November 20, ECB President Christine Lagarde said that AI combined with cyber threat is her primary concern for finance. She described attackers as often anonymous and hard to track, funded by "toxic states" interested in disrupting the world, and argued that policymakers have not paid enough attention to this risk. The statement reflects Lagarde's personal assessment rather than a measured institutional finding.
items.title: Lagarde names AI-powered cyber threats as top financial risk

items.summary: According to job listings posted this week, Apple is building a proactive agentic assistant that would write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on users' behalf. The company frames these plans as an entry into a fast-growing market already pursued by OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta Platforms and others. The move follows what the report describes as the breakout success of Meta's Muse, which it says has drawn consumer attention for making restaurant reservations, booking travel and preparing news briefings; it also notes a proliferation of tools that let AI control Mac computers and program software.
items.title: Apple developing autonomous AI agent for device, app, web and coding tasks

items.summary: Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC intends to stay invested in Anthropic past its initial public offering, with Chris Emanuel, head of GIC's Technology Investment Group, describing the arrangement as 'lifecycle investing' and saying the partnership has grown 'well beyond the check.' The remarks followed Anthropic's record-breaking IPO on Thursday (Nov 19), which raised about US$81.3 billion at a share price of US$83 above its targeted range of US$70 to US$78, with shares closing up 17 per cent at US$97.17 for a fully diluted valuation just below US$1.8 trillion. Bloomberg reported that GIC invested more than US$4.5 billion across Anthropic's last three funding rounds and valued its stake at about US$15 billion at the IPO price; those investments spanned the Series F round in September 2025 (US$13 billion, valuing the company at US$183 billion), the Coatue-led Series G in February (US$30 billion, US$380 billion valuation) and the co-lead role in the Series H round in May (US$65 billion, US$965 billion valuation). Bloomberg figures are estimates. Emanuel noted that GIC also invested in Ode, an AI services company helping enterprises implement Anthropic's technology, and attributed its conviction to Anthropic's technical capabilities and commitment to developing frontier AI safely.
items.title: GIC plans to remain invested in Anthropic beyond its IPO

items.summary: Demonstrators gathered outside Anthropic's San Francisco offices to call for slowing AI development and strict government regulation, chanting that artificial superintelligence should be built at a human pace rather than raced toward. Protesters targeted recursive self-improvement as the mechanism enabling unattended intelligence upgrades, with signs labeling it "Really stupid idea." The rally followed Anthropic's highly anticipated IPO, which drew investor interest despite market jitters and bubble warnings; the company now faces tougher scrutiny from a Democratic-led US Congress next year while rival OpenAI reportedly postponed its own flotation until 2027. Protesters framed their demands around human control over increasingly powerful machines rather than financial metrics.
items.title: Protesters outside Anthropic's San Francisco offices demand human-controlled AI development

items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Anthropic listed on Nasdaq under the ANT symbol with an IPO price of 83 dollars a share; shares closed up 17 percent at 97.17 dollars, giving the company a market value near 1.77 trillion dollars. The article attributes rising valuations for early investors to this listing but explicitly notes these figures are estimated holding values, not realized profits from selling shares. Bloomberg's estimates put Lightspeed Venture Partners' stake worth about 28 billion dollars (after investing over 3.5 billion), Iconiq above 26 billion (invested over 6 billion), Menlo Ventures near 22 billion, Coatue Management at 16 billion, Singapore's GIC around 15 billion, and Spark Capital and Sound Ventures each about 11 billion dollars. Amazon holds roughly 15 percent and Google roughly 14 percent after the IPO plus a 2.6 billion dollar private placement; both also have business partnerships with Anthropic for its AI models and services. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt's stake, invested in 2021 when valuation was about 461 million dollars, is estimated at around 15 billion dollars on IPO terms. The piece adds that OpenAI may list next year.
items.title: Anthropic's record IPO lifted valuations of its early investors, per Bloomberg estimates

items.summary: At a TomorrowX Summit in Austin, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick said he is prepared to bring employees and other tech CEOs/founders to Nvidia's headquarters with megaphones to pressure staff into supporting the reinstatement of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Speaking to investor Antonio Gracias, Kalanick stated 'हमें जेनसन को वापस लाना होगा' (we have to bring Jensen back), but added that the outcome is not in his hands and no date or formal event has been confirmed. He compared the situation to his own 2017 departure from Uber amid workplace-culture and sexual-harassment investigations, noting he had sent Huang a petition demanding his return at Uber; Kalanick said Huang did not reply. Elon Musk likened removing Huang to benching Michael Jordan on a winning team and reiterated an offer for him to work with him, while Greg Brockman and Sam Altman also weighed in on Huang's importance. Investors Ron Conway and Bill Ackman questioned the Nvidia board's decision. Huang has said he is willing to return if the board judges it serves the company, employees, and shareholders; a petition reportedly gathered over 200,000 signatures, but Business Insider reports the board is currently not considering his reinstatement, leaving the outcome unclear.
items.title: Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick proposes protest at Nvidia HQ to demand Jensen Huang's return as CEO

items.summary: Former Perth barrister Lloyd Rayney has filed legal action seeking a court order compelling Meta to disclose the identities of people he believes have defamed him online. The claim is grounded in his background as an advocate whose wife Corryn was murdered in 2007 and who was found not guilty of her murder in 2012, after which he was struck off as a lawyer in 2020.
items.title: Lloyd Rayney sues Meta to force disclosure of online defamers' identities

items.summary: Demonstrators outside Anthropic's San Francisco offices called for authorities to slow AI development and keep humans in control, chanting that artificial superintelligence is not a race to be run at breakneck speed. Protesters targeted recursive self-improvement as a risky mechanism letting systems upgrade their own intelligence without human oversight, with signs reading 'Ban RSI' and labelling it a really stupid idea. The rally followed Anthropic's highly anticipated IPO, which drew investors despite market jitters and bubble warnings; the company now faces tougher scrutiny from a Democratic-led US Congress next year while rival OpenAI reportedly postponed its own flotation until 2027. Protesters framed their demands around strict government regulation, public accountability, and guaranteeing humans never relinquish control over increasingly powerful machines.
items.title: Protesters in San Francisco demand government regulation of AI after Anthropic's IPO

items.summary: Anthropic PBC closed its Nasdaq debut at $97.17, down roughly 5 per cent in post-market trading as the company completed a record-setting offering of about $107.3 billion that surpassed SpaceX's June raise; the decline pared an intraday surge to nearly 39 per cent above the $83 IPO price and reduced its debut pop from 17 per cent, which occurred against a Nasdaq drop of 2.2 per cent as global stocks headed toward their longest losing streak since September 2023. The offering was oversubscribed about seven times with heavy demand outside the US, including $3 billion sought by Japanese investors and $1.1 billion from UK and continental European retail buyers; Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and other banks earned a record $550 million in fees. Anthropic became the world's seventh-largest public company at roughly $1.8 trillion fully diluted value, lifting its seven founders' combined wealth to about $166 billion while vaulting it as an AI industry leader. The article attributes the after-hours weakness partly to competitive threats such as Apple developing its own autonomous agent and to broader nervousness over Nvidia's role following leadership changes and a midterm Democratic sweep that could reshape regulation, though these are presented as contributing factors rather than proven causes of the decline; analysts also note investors may have sold other positions to buy Anthropic shares. The company reported run-rate revenue of $81 billion as of October 31, up about $10 billion from September, with more than 11,900 customers generating roughly $100,000 each on a trailing twelve-month basis; it posted a $567 million operating loss in the third quarter driven by about $5 billion of computing costs and $2 billion of non-cash charges. Goldman Sachs analysts project positive annual free cash flow only by 2030 while modelling revenue reaching roughly $685 billion that year, contingent on fending off pricing pressure from cheaper open-weight models including Chinese developers; Anthropic could join the Russell 1000 and Nasdaq 100 as early as December if it qualifies for inclusion. No table of figures is presented in this item.
items.title: Anthropic shares fall after record IPO debut amid AI selloff

items.summary: In George and Mattsson (forthcoming), a 91% salary increase for junior village secretaries in Telangana, India raised monthly pay from INR 15,000 to INR 28,719 on 15 July 2021. Using a difference-in-differences design comparing villages led by promoted 'junior' secretaries with those led by unchanged 'regular' secretaries, the authors found no improvement in performance: supervisor scores rose less than half a point over an 18-month window (ruling out even a half-point gain), and auditor and citizen ratings followed the same pattern. Corruption proxies showed no change; dishonesty actually increased slightly as self-reported scores rose 0.4 points on unverifiable indicators. Retention was the sole responsive outcome: secretaries who would otherwise have left at an estimated rate of 16% instead departed at about 2.4 percentage points lower, cutting the annual resignation rate by roughly one point from a base near 5%. High performers were no more likely to stay than low performers, and retention gains came entirely from men; women's rates did not change because they had fewer well-paid outside options. The authors attribute the null performance effect to weak dismissal risk under four-year contracts, which undermines efficiency-wage incentives, plus offsetting responses: 17% of secretaries who complained about pay raised effort after the raise while those preoccupied with promotion reduced it as pay compression narrowed promotion rewards. Of expert forecasts from 85 academics and policy professionals expecting improved performance, reduced corruption, and higher retention of top performers, only the prediction that more secretaries would stay was confirmed.
items.title: Nearly doubling Indian village secretaries' pay improved retention but not performance or honesty

items.summary: On Thursday, Brazil's Justice Ministry ordered formal recognition of permanent possession by the Mebengokre-Kayapo and Yudja-Juruna peoples of the 362,000-hectare (895,000-acre) Kapot Nhinore territory along the Xingu River on the border between Para and Mato Grosso states. President Lula da Silva visited the territory during a public event streamed on the government's YouTube channel; he said privately to Raoni Metuktire that they were legally recognizing his land. The order was issued Thursday, though demarcation remains incomplete because about 200 rural properties overlap the territory, which Lula said would be resolved "once and for all." The territory spans 362,000 hectares (895,000 acres) across roughly 60 people. Greenpeace Brazil's Danicley Aguiar called it a victory to celebrate given Raoni's status as the most celebrated forest defender; Márcio Santilli of the Socioenvironmental Institute described it as significant both as Raoni's birthplace and as protection for rainforest along the Xingu, noting it is one of few stretches outside protected areas that land grabbers and loggers have occupied. Indigenous territories are cited by researchers as effective deforestation curbs: a 2022 MapBiomas analysis found Brazil's Indigenous territories lost just 1% of native vegetation over three decades versus 20% on private land nationwide, though this is an estimate rather than established fact. The Kapot Nhinore territory has faced pressure from soybean farmers and cattle ranchers; a Greenpeace report released Wednesday found about 17% of its forest cleared since 1988. Greenpeace advocated that Brazil's banking authorities change rural lending rules to ease agribusiness pressure on occupied Indigenous territories. The government formally defined the boundaries in 2023, as part of an administrative process begun in 2004. Raoni, diagnosed with cancer at 94 and receiving palliative care since September, toured with Sting and met King Charles III; he reaffirmed support for Lula, who won a fourth term in October.
items.title: Brazil formally recognizes Raoni Metuktire's Kapot Nhinore Indigenous Territory

items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Apple is building an agentic AI assistant capable of writing and debugging code, browsing the web, controlling apps and navigating its operating systems on a user's behalf. The plans were detailed in job listings posted this week for a senior engineering manager overseeing the effort, which quotes describe as creating an agent that "browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code." Apple has reportedly eyed introducing the service by the end of next year, though development remains early. The reporting came after Meta's Muse gained consumer attention for booking travel and reservations; shares of Meta fell nearly 2% and Anthropic more than 3% in late trading following Bloomberg's report on Apple's efforts. Competitors are also advancing agents: OpenAI expanded Dots, Anthropic widened testing of Duet, Google overhauled Tasks to allow phone calls like Musk's Grok Bot, and Google Gemini added computer-use functionality earlier this week. Separately, the beta macOS 27.3 release increased steps for enabling third-party computer-use tools from four to fourteen, a change some see as competition protection amid Apple's ongoing US Justice Department lawsuit over blocking third-party access; meanwhile iOS 27.3 deepens Siri integration with apps but does not yet match a full autonomous agent.
items.title: Apple developing autonomous AI agent to control devices, apps and code

items.summary: Months before Anthropic's record-setting IPO, Palantir CEO Alex Karp criticized frontier AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI for pushing businesses toward dependence on their models. In a CNBC interview, Karp said "We have people trying to drug addict us to a future they [frontier AI models] believe they control," arguing that enterprises should retain ownership of data, infrastructure, and models rather than transferring value to third-party providers as part of Palantir's 'AI sovereignty' campaign. He characterized Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's vision as one "where we own nothing... where our adversaries win." The remarks drew support from Chamath Palihapitiya, who said Karp "deserves a medal," and Satya Nadella, while Jamie Dimon emphasized that companies would ultimately prioritize return on investment. Anthropic responded through Amodei's statement reaffirming its commitment to safety and human control, calling the industry a "race to the top." The comments also touched open-weight models—backed by Palantir in an July letter with Nvidia and Microsoft—and Karp's claim that frontier models derived value from distilling internet and enterprise intellectual property. These remarks gained renewed attention after Anthropic's IPO valued the company at nearly $2 trillion, with shares closing at $97.17, up 17% from its $83 offering price; Amodei stated this "strengthens our resolve to do the right thing." The figures are reported as facts by the article rather than forecasts.
items.title: Palantir CEO Alex Karp accused frontier AI labs of 'drugging' enterprises into dependency, resurfacing after Anthropic's IPO

items.summary: Jon McCormack retired from Apple at the end of October after more than eight years heading its Camera and Photos apps and underlying image-capture technology. No direct vice-president successor was named; his responsibilities are being absorbed by former deputies reporting to Sebastien Marineau-Mes, who now leads AI-integration efforts across Apple's operating systems, while key leaders such as Alok Deshpande remain on the camera team. McCormack oversaw features including the redesigned selfie camera with the iPhone 17 lineup and a variable-aperture camera on the iPhone 18 Pro models, plus a customizable professional Camera app interface during his tenure. He was known internally as an opponent of generative AI for creating or substantially altering photographs, telling Wired that "A photograph is of something that actually happened"; however, people familiar with the matter said his retirement was not tied to any disagreement over Apple's AI strategy. His departure adds to a period of transition in software engineering under Craig Federighi and joins Jennifer Bailey among vice presidents who left this fall, as new CEO John Ternus pursues efficiency-focused management changes.
items.title: Jon McCormack, Apple's iPhone camera-software chief, retires after eight years

items.summary: Deutsche Lufthansa plans to eliminate 1,000 full-time positions at Munich and Frankfurt hubs as part of an effort to reverse losses in the unprofitable Lufthansa Airlines mainline unit. The cuts are set out in a management letter seen by Bloomberg and accompany planned capacity reductions on short- and medium-haul routes plus a fleet shift from Airbus A320 aircraft to smaller A220s. These measures mark the second round of job cuts in slightly more than a year, following an announcement in September 2025 that the group would cut 4,000 administrative jobs by 2030. Lufthansa Airlines reported an operating loss of €180 million (S$254.8 million) over the first nine months, and management attributed worsening conditions to high jet-fuel prices, Middle East conflict, a nine-day strike period, and elevated costs. The measures were revealed on Nov 20 amid ongoing negotiations with labour unions, though no agreement has been reached.
items.title: Lufthansa to cut 1,000 jobs at its mainline airline unit

items.summary: A New York Times report says Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in its largest public offering on record, selling 980 million shares at $83 each under ticker ANT; shares opened at $111.50. The article reports that some employees began buying homes months before the listing using expected shareholdings as backing and could sell about 10 percent of holdings on the first trading day. Real estate agents expect many to move into larger family-friendly homes in San Francisco neighbourhoods such as Noe Valley, Cole Valley and Potrero Hill, often through limited liability companies for privacy; this is contrasted with Facebook's 2012 listing, when engineers were seen driving expensive sports cars. Wealth managers report clients now asking about houses, furniture and helping relatives rather than luxury spending, though the article cautions that luxury spending may not disappear entirely. Seven co-founders have pledged to give away 80 percent of their equity, and Anthropic matches staff commitments to charitable causes; Wild Animal Initiative has received donations of about $100,000 and $50,000 from employees and is in talks over contributions worth millions, while the company announced $50 million in grants for local causes by end of 2027 and plans a public benefit fund starting with 5 percent of its shares. The windfall lands in an expensive market: San Francisco's median house price rose 29 percent to $2.39 million over a year, luxury sales hit nine homes above $10 million and 40 above $5 million in one month, mayor Daniel Lurie declared a rent emergency after apartment prices rose 26 percent, and some rent-controlled tenants are being offered large payments to leave; Redfin estimated that Anthropic and OpenAI employees could collectively afford nearly a third of homes in the San Francisco metro area, though this figure combines both companies and is hypothetical. Tipping Point Community's chief executive Sam Cobbs said he expected greater contributions but had not seen signs of broader commitment, and noted Anthropic gave nonprofits free access to its AI tools for six months before charging.
items.title: Anthropic's record IPO and how employees plan to use their wealth

items.summary: Bloomberg ranked Anthropic as the world's seventh most valuable publicly traded company, with a closing fully diluted valuation of about $1.8 trillion on its Thursday Nasdaq debut; Apple ($5.1 trillion), Microsoft ($3.7 trillion), Nvidia ($3.5 trillion), Alphabet ($3.3 trillion) and Amazon ($2.8 trillion) ranked higher, followed by SpaceX at $1.9 trillion. Shares opened at $111.50 (about 34% above the $83 IPO price), then pared gains to close at $97.17, up 17% from the offer price; the opening price briefly implied a valuation of about $2 trillion using roughly 18 billion shares including options and RSUs. The listing marked a sharp rise from an estimated $183 billion valuation around 14 months earlier, after Anthropic had sought slightly more than $1 trillion during its November roadshow. Profit-taking followed the early surge as investors weighed prospects against concerns over high AI valuations, infrastructure spending and long-term profitability; analyst Bob O'Donnell of TECHnalysis Research said stability would depend on OpenAI's performance, Nvidia developments, data center policy and Anthropic's historical results. Led by CEO Dario Amodei (a former OpenAI employee), the company reported 47% quarter-over-quarter revenue growth in Q3 with a narrowing net loss, holds nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with partners including Amazon and Google, and has indicated it may use debt toward investment-grade status. The valuation is based on Bloomberg's closing-price ranking of fully diluted market values; the figures are reported claims from Reuters and Bloomberg rather than independently verified data.
items.title: Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO valuation after profit-taking

items.summary: US semiconductor equipment maker KLA opened Building 22B in Ang Mo Kio, giving it roughly 210,000 sq ft of new operational space; the site was announced in October 2024 and is now fully operational. The company has outlined plans for a further expansion phase that would be larger than this one, but those details are still being defined pending finalised land arrangements and approvals, so no third-phase commitment or timeline is established. Kneepkens said the next phase “will be bigger than the current expanded site.” Long-term, Building 22B and the planned phase could support about 1,000 new jobs across R&D, supply chain and manufacturing engineering; KLA Singapore currently employs over 2,200 people on multiple shifts. Higgins attributed growth to local talent, collaborative partners and supplier/customer access, and said demand is “only accelerating.” The expansion follows investment commitments from other semiconductor value-chain firms including GlobalFoundries, Micron, Siltronic, Soitec, UMC, Vanguard International Semiconductor and NXP Semiconductors. Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong noted Singapore accounts for around one-fifth of global production and has committed $800 million under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 plan to RIE Flagship in Semiconductors; he also cited a three-year KLA–A*STAR collaboration and local supplier Sys-Mac Automation Engineering. The opening was attended by Singapore Economic Development Board executive vice-president Cindy Koh.
items.title: KLA opens expanded Singapore plant with plans for a third expansion phase

items.summary: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting adopted a document titled 'APEC Trade Digitalization Cooperation Framework (2027-2030)' on Thursday, per the meeting's release. The framework covers trade digitalization for the period spanning 2027 to 2030; its specific contents are not detailed in the item beyond this title and date range. A photograph accompanying the announcement shows an 'APEC China 2026' sign at Shenzhen International Exchange Center, dated November 19, 2026.
items.title: APEC adopts Trade Digitalization Cooperation Framework (2027-2030)

items.summary: Pakistani think-tank analyst Khurram Abbas alleged on X that India did not extend the customary welcome to Pakistan climate change and environmental coordination minister Musadik Masood Malik, who arrived in New Delhi on Thursday for the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum. ANI cited official sources contradicting this claim, reporting that a director from the Union ministry of culture and an under secretary from the MEA's Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran (PAI) division were present at the airport to receive Malik as part of welcome protocol. The same sources stated all SCO member countries arriving in New Delhi received similar treatment. Malik is described as the first Pakistani minister to visit India since 2023 and the first such trip following the May 2025 military confrontation after the Pahalgam terror attack, which killed 26 people; his last high-profile counterpart was foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari in 2023. Abbas's post characterised him as a Pakistani climate change and environmental coordination minister arriving to attend an SCO meeting, welcomed by the Pakistani CdA. The forum runs November 20-22, with Pakistan representing Islamabad on dialogue among civilisations; MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed invitations extended to all 10 member states plus observers and partners.
items.title: ANI contradicts Pakistani analyst's claim that no Indian official welcomed Musadik Malik in Delhi

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday dismissed Karnataka's appeal against a state high court ruling that allows bike taxi operations across the state, leaving in place an order benefiting Ola, Uber, Rapido, motorcycle owners and the Bike Taxi Welfare Association. The high court permitted motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles and used as contract carriages provided they meet the state's regulatory requirements.
items.title: Supreme Court upholds Karnataka HC order permitting bike taxi services

items.summary: A CGTN video segment, reported by Mark Niu and promoted via a cookie consent notice and newsletter sign-up, frames artificial intelligence as a major topic at the ongoing APEC meetings.
